chunks: No one but Aban ibn Abi Ayyash has narrated from him. And in his book there are notorious unrecognized (things). And I do not deem it to be but fabricated.

key_terms.أَبَانُ بْنُ أَبِي عَيَّاشٍ: Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, a primary narrator from Sulaym.
key_terms.الْكِتَابِ: The book, referring to Sulaym's work.
key_terms.سَلِيمُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ الْهَلَالِيُّ: Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali, a companion of the Imams.
key_terms.مَنْكَرَاتٌ: Ankarat, narrations that are weak or unknown, often contradicting established reports.

ai.seo_question: What is the status of Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali's book in Shia hadith sciences?
ai.summary: This entry from Kitab al-Du'afa discusses the narrator Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali. It notes that he was primarily narrated from by Aban ibn Abi Ayyash and that his book contains well-known weak or unrecognized narrations, leading the author to believe it is likely fabricated (mawdu').
